blocks.text: Dear Mr. Wallace:

This letter records the terms on which our firm will act for {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}} in the integration work that follows the recent merger, and, once you have countersigned it, it will stand as the agreement between us. I have set it down in plain terms, so that it reads as an account of what we discussed together rather than as an instrument to be construed against either of us, and I would ask you to read it against that conversation and to tell me, before you sign, if any part of it sits at odds with how you remember what was said.
The Work We Will Undertake

We will help the leadership of {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}} bring the two organizations that the merger has joined into a single operating whole, and we will do so in the deliberate sequence that such work rewards: first understanding how each side runs today, then agreeing where the combined business ought to run differently, and only then setting the changes in motion in an order that the organization can absorb without losing a step. Our concern throughout is that the integration deliver the value the transaction was meant to create, and that it do so without unsettling the parts of either business that are already working well.

The engagement covers the operating model, the near-term cost questions that a combination of this kind always raises, and a practical plan for the first months of the joined enterprise, and it extends to our counsel on the decisions those questions force. It does not extend to the running of the company, which remains yours, nor to legal, tax, or accounting advice, on which you should continue to rely on the advisers who ordinarily provide it; where our work touches those matters, what we offer is a considered view and not a professional opinion in their place.

Our way of working is unhurried and, I hope, plain in its manner. We begin by listening, to your leadership and to the people on both sides of the merger who already carry a view of how the work is done, before we commit any recommendation to paper; we then set down the small number of decisions that the integration truly turns on, and we build the rest of the plan outward from those. When the ground moves under the work, as it does in every combination of two going concerns, we will come back to you and adjust the plan with you and not around you.
Who Will Carry the Work

Jason Torres, a Principal of the firm, will own the relationship with you and will be the person to whom you bring any question of substance; he is accustomed to telling a client what the evidence shows and not what is easiest to hear, and you should expect that of him. Working to him, Daniel Leach and Mary Parker will carry much of the day-to-day analysis, Daniel on the operating and cost data and Mary on the background research that grounds our recommendations, and each of them will see to it that any figure we place in front of you can be traced back to where it came from.

I will keep my own hand on the engagement, particularly at the points where a judgment must be made about how far a recommendation can be pressed before it outruns what we actually know, and nothing of consequence will leave the firm under our name without my having read it first. You are welcome to reach me directly at any time, though for most matters Jason Torres will be the quicker route to an answer.
Fee and Invoicing

Our fee for the engagement as I have described it is {{fact:f:E-2009-003.fee}}, which covers the time of the people named above through the expected close of the work. We will render invoices against that amount as the engagement proceeds, and each will be payable within thirty days of your receipt of it. The fee covers our people and their time and not the incidental costs of the work, such as travel or the reproduction of materials, which we will incur only with your agreement and pass through to you at what they cost us; should the shape of the work change materially from what this letter contemplates, I will raise the question of the fee with you and we will settle it together before the further work begins, so that nothing reaches you on an invoice as a surprise.
Term and Termination

The engagement begins on {{fact:f:E-2009-003.start}} and is expected to run for something on the order of four months, though we will treat it as complete when the work is genuinely done and not merely when the calendar has turned. Either of us may bring it to an end on fourteen days' written notice to the other; if you choose to do so, you will owe us for the work properly performed to that point and for any costs already committed on your behalf, and for nothing beyond that.
Confidentiality

Everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}} and the businesses it has combined we will hold in confidence and use only for the purposes of this engagement. That obligation binds every member of our team, it survives the end of our work, and it covers the fact of our involvement as fully as it covers its substance. We ask the same of you in respect of the methods and the written materials we share with you, which represent the firm's own way of working.
Limitation of Liability

We will perform the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of a firm engaged for it, and we stand behind what we do. We do not, however, control the decisions that the leadership of the combined company will ultimately take, nor the conditions of the markets in which it operates, and so, save to the extent the law does not permit such a limit, our liability to you arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established, and any dispute arising under it will be determined by the courts of that state. Should any single provision of this letter be held unenforceable, the remainder of it will continue in force, unaffected.

If this letter reflects the understanding we reached, I would be grateful if you would sign one copy where indicated below and return it to us, keeping the other for your own file. Once your signed copy is in our hands, Daniel Leach will write to you to fix the first meetings and the initial requests for information, so that we can begin without delay.

The purpose of this memo is to set out what each of us owns as the post-merger integration for {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}} gets under way, so that we begin in step and not at cross purposes. The engagement commenced on {{fact:f:E-2009-003.start}} and is expected to run for about four months; our sponsor on the client side is Joseph Wallace, the Chief Financial Officer, and Jason Torres will be our single point of contact with him so that the client hears one voice from us. In this first phase the aim is narrow and practical: to understand how each of the two combined businesses runs today before we form any view about how the joined company should run tomorrow. What this phase produces is a shared and evidenced picture of the current state, together with a first read on where the value of the combination actually sits; it does not produce recommendations, which come later and only once the client has agreed the facts they rest on.
The work, by area

items: Current-state map of the two operating models. I will document how each side runs today across the core functions, drawing on the organization charts, the existing process documentation, and a short round of interviews, and note where the two overlap or pull against each other.

Cost and finance baseline. Working with the client's finance team under Joseph Wallace, I will assemble a clean baseline of the combined cost structure, so that any later recommendation rests on figures both sides accept.

Market and peer context. Mary Parker will build the background on the combined company's markets and closest peers, with the sources kept on file, to frame where the integration can create the most value.
Integration priorities and sequencing. Jason Torres will lead the early view on which decisions the integration turns on and the order in which the organization can absorb them.

Working record. We will keep a shared engagement file from the first week, so that every figure and source we rely on can be traced, and so that our notes to the client draw from one record and not from memory.

blocks.text: What happens next

For the coming week the priority is access and materials. I will send the client team the initial request for information today, and Mary Parker will begin the market and peer scan in parallel so that we are not idle while the data comes in; Jason Torres will confirm the cadence of the standing check-ins with Joseph Wallace and circulate the schedule to all of us. The single thing I need from each of you before we meet again is your list of the documents and contacts your area will require, sent to me by the end of the week, so that I can fold it into one request to the client and not several. I will keep the shared engagement file current as material arrives and post a short index of what we have received and what is still outstanding, so that no one has to ask me twice for the same status, and so that Jason Torres has an accurate picture before each check-in with Joseph Wallace.
Good morning Joseph,

The current-state review for {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}} is on schedule, and I am writing chiefly to line up the data we will need for the next stage and to confirm the working session we discussed. Mary Parker has finished the first pass on the market and peer material, and I have most of the operating-model documentation in hand; the gap now is on the finance side, where three of the cost schedules we requested have not yet reached us from your team.

For the record, the attendee list for the session is Jason Torres, Mary Parker, and Daniel Leach from our side, with Joseph Wallace and the owners of the cost schedules from yours. Jason Torres will take everyone through the current-state findings, so it will help to have the people who maintain those schedules in the room and able to speak to them.
Could you have the three outstanding schedules sent to me by the middle of next week? With those in hand we can hold the session as planned and keep the review on its timeline.
Sincerely

blocks.text: Good morning Joseph,

Thank you: the outstanding cost schedules reached us this morning, so we now have what we need for the working session on the {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}} integration. Ahead of it, we have gathered the early findings into a short briefing deck, which I will send under separate cover for your team to read before we meet. The deck lists Mary Parker and Daniel Leach as its preparers, so any question on the underlying figures can come to either of us.

Jason Torres will lead the session itself and would welcome a short conversation with you, Joseph Wallace, beforehand, to settle on the two or three decisions we believe the integration turns on before the wider group convenes.
If you can let me know a half hour that suits you and Jason Torres in the next day or two, I will hold it and send the agenda around to everyone by the end of the week.
Sincerely
Minutes of the Working Session: Post-Merger Integration for {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}}

These minutes record the working session held with the client team to review the current-state findings and to agree the priorities for the next phase of the integration for {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}}.
Attendees

items: 1. Jason Torres, Principal, Calderwood Partners (chair)
2. Daniel Leach, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners
3. Mary Parker, Research Associate, Calderwood Partners
4. Joseph Wallace, Chief Financial Officer, {{fact:f:E-2009-003.client}}

blocks.text: Discussion

The session opened with a review of the current-state work, which is now substantially complete. Daniel Leach walked the group through the map of the two operating models as they run today, observing that the greatest overlap sits in the shared support functions and that the customer-facing operations differ more than either side had assumed at the outset; the group agreed that this difference is the area most likely to reward careful handling, since a hasty consolidation there would risk disturbing revenue that is presently sound.

On the finance side, Joseph Wallace confirmed that the outstanding cost schedules had been provided, and Daniel Leach reported that the combined cost baseline is now assembled and reconciled against them, with only a small number of allocations still to be agreed between the two finance teams. Mary Parker presented the market and peer context she has compiled, which the group used to frame where the integration might create the most value, and there followed a discussion, left open at the close, of whether the near-term savings identified in the support functions are as substantial in practice as they appear on paper. Joseph Wallace cautioned that some of the apparent duplication reflects contractual commitments that cannot be unwound quickly, and the group accepted that the savings estimate should distinguish what can be realized in the first year from what depends on those commitments running their course.

Before turning to actions, the group set out the questions on which the next phase will turn: the order in which functions should be combined, the savings that can be relied upon as against those that are merely nominal, and the safeguards needed to protect the parts of each business that are already performing well. It was agreed that these questions would be carried into a formal statement of priorities for the client's leadership, and that nothing would be presented as settled until both finance teams had signed off on the underlying figures. Jason Torres noted that the priorities should be framed as choices for the leadership to make rather than as conclusions from us, since the decisions that follow are theirs to own, and the group agreed to keep the analysis and the recommendation clearly separate in whatever is put in front of them.
Action items

rows: Agree the remaining cost allocations with the two finance teams and close the combined baseline
Circulate the compiled market and peer context to the client's leadership
Confirm the delivered schedules are complete and nominate the finance owner for the allocation sign-off
Draft the statement of priorities for the next phase and set the next review with the client

blocks.text: The next working session will be scheduled once the priorities are drafted. These minutes will stand as the record of what was agreed unless a correction is raised within the week.
